I farm only 3.1 mu, and at my age I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all of it because it is the system I know best, it fits our land and water, and it keeps the work predictable. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield, but I will not manage too intensively because labor in the family is limited and some people work off-farm. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed, moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and simple rotary tillage, because I want stable output and manageable fieldwork. For maize, I will use hybrid seed for better yield, give a bit more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate in key periods, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed. I am not chasing the highest possible yield; I am aiming for a steady, familiar plan that I can carry through reliably this year.
